statement_record.book: Lemma 5.10 (two-pullbacks lemma). For two adjacent commuting squares over a composable bottom row A -> B -> C: (1) if both squares are pullbacks then the outer rectangle is a pullback (hence A x_B (B x_C D) ≅ A x_C D); (2) if the RIGHT square and the OUTER rectangle are pullbacks then the LEFT square is a pullback.

statement_record.book: Corollary 5.11. Given a commutative triangle beta ∘ gamma = alpha over C and any h : C' -> C, with pullbacks alpha' : A' -> C' of alpha and beta' : B' -> C' of beta along h, there is a UNIQUE gamma' : A' -> B' making the prism commute — beta' ∘ gamma' = alpha' (left face a commutative triangle) and the upper face (A'->A, gamma', gamma, B'->B) a commutative rectangle — and moreover that upper square is itself a pullback.
statement_record.intree: Star_Functor's fmap: for a slice arrow (g; H) : (a; x) ~> (b; y) over the base, gamma' := unique_obj uniq where uniq := ump_pullbacks y f ypb _ (g ∘ pullback_fst x f xpb) (pullback_snd x f xpb) _ ; its `unique_property` gives BOTH `pullback_fst y f ypb ∘ gamma' ≈ g ∘ pullback_fst x f xpb` (upper rectangle commutes) and `pullback_snd y f ypb ∘ gamma' ≈ pullback_snd x f xpb` (beta' ∘ gamma' ≈ alpha'), and `uniqueness` gives uniqueness among arrows satisfying both.
statement_record.strength_comparison: intree-weaker. The existence/uniqueness half of the corollary is realized (it is exactly the pullback UMP applied to the cone (gamma ∘ alpha'-leg, alpha'), and both prism commutations plus uniqueness are the two components of `unique_property`/`uniqueness`), but only INSIDE the fmap field of Star_Functor — there is no standalone lemma named for it. The distinctive extra clause that makes 5.11 a corollary of the two-pullbacks lemma — that the upper square (A'->A, gamma', gamma, B'->B) is ITSELF a pullback — is not proved anywhere in the tree, although [pullback_unpaste] supplies it in one step.

statement_record.book: Corollary 5.13. For C with pullbacks and f : A -> B, the square of categories formed by f^-1 : Sub(B) -> Sub(A), f* : C/B -> C/A and the two inclusions Sub(-) -> C/(-) commutes, since f^-1 is by definition the restriction of f*. In particular f^-1 is functorial, i.e. monotone for inclusion (M ⊆ N ⇒ f^-1 M ⊆ f^-1 N); hence M ≡ N ⇒ f^-1 M ≡ f^-1 N and f^-1 descends to f^-1/≡ : Sub(B)/≡ -> Sub(A)/≡.

The inclusion preorder exists separately as `sub_le` in Theory/Subobject.v, with `sub_equiv_iff_mutual : (u ≈ v) ↔ (sub_le u v * sub_le v u)`.

statement_record.book: Example 5.14. In Sets: (i) the pullback E = {(a,b) | f a = g b} is the equalizer of f∘pi1 and g∘pi2 : A x B -> C; (ii) with B = 1, C = 2, g = true, U ⊆ A is the pullback of true : 1 -> 2 along chi_U; (iii) the bijection 2^A ≅ P(A) sends phi to V_phi = phi^-1(true), described as a pullback; (iv) for f : B -> A, f^-1 : P(A) -> P(B) is pullback, and the two-pullbacks lemma gives f^-1(V_phi) = V_{phi ∘ f} — substitution is pullback; (v) hence the square with 2^f on one edge and f^-1 on the other commutes: the iso 2^A ≅ P(A) is NATURAL in A, strictly stronger than a pointwise bijection.

statement_record.book: Definition 5.17. A diagram of type J in C is a functor D : J ⟶ C. A cone to D is an object C with arrows c_j : C -> D_j, one per object j of J, such that D_alpha ∘ c_i = c_j for every alpha : i -> j in J. A morphism of cones theta : (C, c_j) -> (C', c'_j) is an arrow theta : C -> C' with c_j = c'_j ∘ theta for all j. Cones to D and their morphisms form a category Cone(D).
statement_record.intree: ACone c F := { vertex_map (x : J) : c ~> F x; cone_coherence (f : x ~> y) : fmap[F] f ∘ vertex_map x ≈ vertex_map y };  Cone F := { vertex_obj : C; coneFrom : ACone vertex_obj F };  Cones F : Category with hom N L := { u : vertex_obj[N] ~> vertex_obj[L] & ∀ j, vertex_map[L] ∘ u ≈ vertex_map[N] j }.
statement_record.strength_comparison: same, with a faithful setoid rephrasing (= becomes ≈, and cone morphisms are identified when their apex maps agree, the commutation witness being proof-irrelevant). Every clause matches: diagram = functor (the library uses `F : J ⟶ C` directly as the diagram — there is no separate `Diagram` abbreviation, which is a naming difference only); the cone coherence field is literally D_alpha ∘ c_i ≈ c_j; the hom of Cones F is literally an apex map with the triangle equations c_j ≈ c'_j ∘ theta; identity and composition are the apex identity and composite.
